anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the engine-configuration layer, where runtime parameters governing memory pools, checkpoint cadence, log sizing, background workers, parallelism, isolation, and durability are not calibrated to the hardware capacity, workload mix, or version-specific defaults. It is distinct from the resource layers it controls because the failure originates from the parameter setting itself rather than from the underlying physical resource truly reaching its limit. Observable phenomena: wait-event distribution that does not match hardware utilization, such as heavy log-write waits while the storage device is idle or sustained CPU spinning while cores are not saturated, checkpoint or page-flush storms triggered immediately after a configuration change, background cleanup falling behind despite a low data-modification rate, and workload regressions appearing right after upgrades, instance resizing, or manual tuning. Possible contributing factors: buffer-pool size mismatched to available memory, per-session work memory set too high or too low for the concurrency level, checkpoint-cadence and transaction-log size parameters not aligned with the redo generation rate, cleanup-worker thresholds not aligned with the data-modification rate, parallelism limits over- or under-provisioned for the available cores, connection limits set beyond what per-session memory can sustain, and version-default changes silently altering semantics after upgrades.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits for additional data from a connection longer than net_read_timeout.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
